thread:
maria_support: Customer (org_id: org_9a7) reports monthly bucket hit 0 at ~23:58 local time and got 429s. UI showed 0 until 00:00:35 local, then jumped to full. Can someone confirm expected behaviour?
alex_infra: Do we have any known issues with refill timing or UI cache lag?
maria_support: Customer attached screenshot and logs. Header shows tenant TZ = America/Los_Angeles. They say refill should be midnight PST and it apparently happened ~00:00:35.
jordan_billing: FYI billing refill job historically runs at tenant-local midnight, but we migrated a large batch to UTC-normalized refill logic last quarter. Need org id + plan to confirm any exception.
maria_support: org_9a7 on Growth annual. API log snippet they pasted: 
```
[2025-02-10T07:58:12Z] 429 POST /v1/completions org=org_9a7 token_usage=1200
[2025-02-10T07:58:14Z] 429 POST /v1/completions org=org_9a7 token_usage=1100
[2025-02-10T08:00:35Z] 200 POST /admin/recharge org=org_9a7 credited=500000
[2025-02-10T08:00:35Z] 200 GET /v1/usage org=org_9a7 remaining=500000
```
sam_sre: That log shows the refill processed at 08:00:35Z which is 00:00:35 PST. Two things jump out: 1) the recharge job has jitter (we spread tenants to avoid thundering herd) and 2) UI cache key tenant_quota_{org} TTL might still be serving stale zero value.
alex_infra: We rolled a config change in Jan that increased UI quota cache TTL to 60s. Previously it was 15s. That plus the job jitter explains ~35s visible delay.
deploy-bot: deploybot: rollout/refresh-cache-config v2 -> canary deployed to 2 hosts :rocket: 
alex_infra: I can repro in staging: force refill at 08:00:00Z and because of jitter the job fires at 08:00:30-09Z window; UI continues to show zero until cache invalidation. Root cause = (jitter up to 45s) + longer TTL.
jordan_billing: Customer is upset — is this considered an SLA miss? If refill is promised at tenant local midnight we should treat >30s as a problem.
maria_support: Customer is asking for explanation and a fix. For immediate remediation I can grant a goodwill 1-day token credit. Should we communicate jitter behaviour?
alex_infra: Proposal: reduce jitter to max 15s for tenants with local-midnight contracts, and lower UI quota cache TTL to 10s in canary. Also add a fast path: when recharge job completes for a tenant, publish a cache-bust event so UI refreshes immediately.
sam_sre: Adding monitoring: emit metric recharge_lag_seconds = refill_time - tenant_local_midnight and tag with tenant_id. Alert if >10s for >5% of active tenants in a region for 1h. Also adding a log field local_midnight_expected and actual_refill_ts for easier postmortems.
jordan_billing: I'll draft an email apologizing, explain that refills can incur brief delay (we're targeting <15s) and confirm the 1-day credit.
maria_support: Customer accepted the credit and explanation. I'll file internal follow-up INF-4321 to track reducing jitter and cache TTL and to implement cache-bust events. Closing the support case. :white_check_mark: 
alex_infra: Implemented TTL change in canary, reduced jitter config, and added cache-bust event emit in canary. Will watch deploy metrics.
sam_sre: Added log/metric changes and a dashboard panel for refill lag per-tenant.
maria_support: Thanks all. Leaving notes on the ticket for docs update: "recharge can be delayed up to ~60s during heavy churn; working to reduce to <15s" so CS has a clear line.
